$comment: ⛔ THE CASES OF THE `kb/Work/` FRONTMATTER READER (kb/Work PB875, PB245, PB3196, PB2878).
The work register has ONE reader, `parse_frontmatter` in `scripts/spec/work.py`, and `work.py --self-test` is its
test: it reads every case below and compares what the reader SEES with the case's `expect`. The register had two
readers until PB2878 (a C# twin, `WorkRegister.cs`, that the register drift tests used), and for months they read
one file format differently: a list WRAPPED across two lines — the normal YAML shape, carried by kb/Work/PB205 —
was truncated by the Python reader and DISCARDED ENTIRELY by the C# one, so kb/Work/PB390 went on claiming four
inventory rows in the register while the gate that enforces claims saw none, and `work.py check` called the same
note well-formed (kb/Work PB875). The cases stay: they are the shapes the register has actually contained, each of
which broke a reader once, and the reader is still the thing every tool of the register trusts.
Each case is a raw frontmatter TEXT plus the NORMALIZED view the reader must produce. Absent and empty are
deliberately one answer (a missing key says exactly as much as an empty one); a MALFORMED value is a third answer
and carries an error CODE, because collapsing it into 'empty' is the fail-open PB875 is about.
`terminal` is what the DONE vocabulary (`work.TERMINAL_STATUSES`) makes of the status. `work.py --self-test` refuses
a fixture that leaves any status of `work.STATUSES` without a case, or any case without every field the view
reports, so a status added to the vocabulary reaches the reader's answers here before anything can read it
differently (kb/Work PB3196).
`scalars` measures the one-line value reader `_scalar` (kb/Work PB3812): `value` is the text after `key: `, `expect`
the value the reader returns, `error` the code it reports (empty for none). A double-quoted value decodes YAML 1.2
section 5.7's escapes (one case per escape the reader defines, which `--self-test` demands of the whole table), and a
backslash that table lacks or a quote never closed is an error with the text kept as written, never a silent pass.
⚙ ADD A SHAPE HERE THE MOMENT THE REGISTER GROWS ONE. A shape the reader is not measured on is a shape it is free to
misread, and the misreading is invisible until a note happens to use it.

scalars.name: a double-quoted scalar is its text without the quotes
an escaped quote is a quote
an escaped backslash is a backslash
the escape backslash-0 is U+0000
the escape backslash-a is U+0007
the escape backslash-b is U+0008
the escape backslash-t is U+0009
the escape backslash-<tab> is U+0009
the escape backslash-n is U+000A
the escape backslash-v is U+000B
the escape backslash-f is U+000C
the escape backslash-r is U+000D
the escape backslash-e is U+001B
the escape backslash-<space> is U+0020
the escape backslash-/ is U+002F
the escape backslash-N is U+0085
the escape backslash-_ is U+00A0
the escape backslash-L is U+2028
the escape backslash-P is U+2029
the escape backslash-x takes two hex digits
the escape backslash-u takes four hex digits
the escape backslash-U takes eight hex digits
a single-quoted scalar doubles its quote
a single-quoted scalar has no escapes
a plain scalar is as written
a plain scalar keeps its backslash
an empty double-quoted scalar is empty
an escape YAML does not define is an error (backslash-C), the text kept as written
a truncated backslash-x is an unknown escape
an unterminated double quote is an error
a lone quote is an error
an unterminated single quote is an error
